about: The core every Cascade package is built on: it files what arrives in a person's pod, names it, runs the matcher and builds the views. Apps call cascade-runtime, which wraps it; this page is for whoever builds on the core itself.

glossary.definition: of an adapter, to take a document it can read and convert it. The saved-output Bridge declines a document its step marks `unaccepted.txt`, and accepts one it saved nothing for.
one thing done to a pod that writes files to it: an import, an entry session, a connection to a hospital's server, or a run of the matcher.
the program that converts an export into records; `import` loads it on first use.
what the Bridge reads from an adapter before loading it: the media type it converts, and the files of the adapter and of the vocabulary it needs to load.
of an open, to take a newer version of a table the pod uses as the pod's current one.
the slow key derivation that turns a secret into a pod's key, so that guessing a secret costs time.
one state of one record as a source reported it, as an adapter hands it to the runtime, before it is filed.
the address of a hospital server's API, which a record read from that server is named from.
a thing a statement mentions without an IRI, which has no name outside its file.
the program that runs an adapter on a document and returns what it converted, or the reason it failed.
of a pod: its derived state and the files its build writes worked out from every file, with nothing kept from before.
Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture: HL7's standard for the XML summary documents patient portals hand out.
a graph's statements written one to a line in the single spelling and order the W3C's RDFC-1.0 fixes, so equal graphs give equal text.
a path written the one plain way: no `.` or `..` part, no doubled or leading slash, no backslash.
one of the five things `runtime/the-kit.feature` requires of a replay of a kit's story, numbered 2 to 6, such as check 3, "every file conforms to the shapes". Check 1 is that every example passes.
a folder holding a repository at one commit; a sibling checkout is one in the folder beside the runtime's own.
a public database of genetic variants; each has a ClinVar ID.
a published list of codes for one kind of thing, such as RxNorm for medicines, LOINC for lab tests and SNOMED CT for clinical findings.
a query the vocabulary ships under `queries/matcher/` that returns the pairs of records one rule holds to be one thing.
a repository the runtime reads when it runs: the vocabulary, an adapter, the reference tables.
the form of a SPARQL query that returns statements it builds, where SELECT returns rows.
a file named by a hash of what it holds: a document or a version.
what an adapter reports about a document beside its graph, saved as `findings.ttl`: what it left out or could not read. Not a finding for review, which is the pod's.
of a series, the version a pod opened now is given: the newest one the app has kept.
the organisation that keeps a document and answers for its true copy.
a pod as a query reads it: a default graph and named graphs.
the statements a query reads outside any `GRAPH` block.
a query of the vocabulary that adds to a pod's dataset what follows from its files, such as which revision of a record is current.
the file in the pod that says which series a table version belongs to, its number, and which version it revises.
a judgment that its members are separate things; it overrules a Same of the two.
one file of an export, which the pod keeps under the hash of its bytes.
the W3C's Evaluation and Report Language: a report as RDF, one assertion for each test with its outcome.
one call of `pod.enter()`: the act that files what the owner typed, as one owner-entered record or several, under a `urn:uuid:` name the app makes once.
in a feature, one named run: steps on a pod, then what a query of it must return.
what a person downloads of their own records: an Apple Health export, or a C-CDA document from a patient portal.
one sentence a kit check returns, saying one thing wrong with the pod; a check passes when it returns none.
a file of the vocabulary that states rules of a pod and, under each, examples.
something the matcher noticed about a pod's records and filed for the owner to answer with a judgment.
a number the C-CDA adapter works out from the strings of a record that has no id, to tell such records apart.
the parent snapshot that is the same writer's previous snapshot; a writer's first snapshot has none.
a sealed pod, or one sealed file, that the pod encryption vectors carry together with the secrets that open it.
in SHACL, a node a shape is checking.
a set of statements held under a name; each file of a pod is read as the graph named by its address.
in SPARQL, the patterns between one pair of braces. A query's WHERE group is the one its WHERE keyword opens, not one inside a sub-select, OPTIONAL, MINUS or UNION.
a short name a kit gives a record or a judgment, with the inputs its name is made from, in the kit's `handles.json`.
a short code worked out from bytes, such as a file's or the text of an IRI: the same bytes always give the same hash, and any change gives another.
the snapshot of this app's latest act in a pod.
the one file of a sealed pod left readable, `settings/encryption.json`, which says how the pod is sealed.
the standard way to write a genetic variant, such as `NM_000249.4:c.2042C>T`.
the act of bringing an export's documents into a pod; its own file lists the documents it kept.
a file kept beside a version of a reference table that says which rows each code finds, so that the rows need not all be read.
the name of one thing, written as an address, such as `urn:uuid:3b9e2d47-8c15-4f6a-a0d2-7e5c1b9f4a63` or `https://ns.cascadeprotocol.org/cascade#allergen`; it need not be one a browser can open.
of two graphs: the same statements once their blank nodes are matched up.
a conclusion about records, made by a person or by a machine.
the reason a rule gives for a Same, such as "same code".
a pod's dataset held in memory from one step to the next, in place of a new read of every file.
a story and the exports it uses, which the vocabulary carries for testing, such as `alex-rivera`.
the file the build writes that gives each thing in a pod (a record, a version, a revision, a document, a view entry, the subject) one name a person can read.
the vocabulary's file that says in which folder of a pod each kind of thing is filed.
of the kept dataset: changes it in place into the matcher's view for the length of a run, and puts it back after.
a choice of which judgments count when a question is answered: `everyday` is the default, and `export` is stricter, for records sent elsewhere.
a second working folder of one checkout, as `git worktree add` makes.
the file the build writes last, which lists the pod's views and says when they were built.
the part of a runtime that compares a pod's records and writes a Same for those its rules find to be one thing, such as one allergy reported by two sources.
a Same the matcher wrote for records its rules found to be one thing; it names the version of each reference table it used.
a pod as the matcher reads it: its files but those the build writes, with the everyday lens's derived state.
the kind of a document as the web names it, such as `application/fhir+json`.
a record a judgment is about.
a parent snapshot that is another head, taken in as a git merge takes in a branch.
the set hash Bitcoin Core uses: one number for each member, multiplied together modulo a 3072-bit prime, so the order of members does not matter.
a W3C text format that writes one statement a line.
a term of the vocabulary that says how one kind of thing is named, from its content or from listed inputs, such as `cascade:VersionNamingRule`.
a writer with no head, or with one the pod does not hold; its first snapshot has no first parent and merges every head in the pod.
a Gherkin Scenario Outline: one example written once and run for each row of its table.
the person who keeps a pod and decides what its records mean; in every pod on this page, the subject acting for themselves.
one file holding all of a sample's files, so a page fetches them at once.
the snapshot that an act's snapshot names as the one before it; a pod's first snapshot has none.
the person an export's records are about, as that source knows them, before anyone has said who they are in the pod.
the function a replay calls to perform steps of one kind, such as an import or an entry session.
one wording of a step that `runtime/steps.md` defines, such as "the pod holds no revision".
the name a view entry has in a pod's derived state, `urn:cascade:entry:` and a hash, until the build names the entry in its view.
one person's records, and what that person has said about them, kept as files in one folder.
the SHACL engine the vocabulary's own tests run; the results this package gives are held to its.
one statement together with the graph that holds it.
one JavaScript global environment, such as a page or an iframe; an object made in another realm fails `instanceof` here.
of a step with a kept build: only the records the step reached are derived and written again.
one thing said about a person's health, such as an allergy, a medication or a lab result.
public code lists, such as RxNorm for medicines, that tell a runtime when two codes mean one thing.
the error thrown when the package declines a request it understood, such as a name it does not have; it has written no file of the person's.
on a call's result, why a rule turned the call down; a refused call wrote no file of the person's, though a pod with a build still rewrites its manifest.
of a code system, to give it a URI space in the vocabulary, from which a code's IRI is made.
a version of the rule list as shipped; a release may declare an earlier rule wrong.
of a kept store, to replace it with a new store filled from the old one, which frees the memory the old one held.
performing a story's steps, in order, on a new pod.
a union that can undo what a run did to it: it remembers the graphs it dropped, added to or took subjects from, and `restore()` puts every quad and blank node back.
the owner taking back a judgment they filed: the judgment stays in the pod and no longer counts.
the pod's note that a record took a version at one arrival: which version, when, and from which document. (Of a pod, `revision()` is another thing: a name for the state its files are in.)
a numbered requirement in the vocabulary that every runtime must meet, such as A14 in `runtime/arrivals.feature`; a heading on this page links the rules its API reaches.
the vocabulary's list of what the matcher compares, each line naming a query and the table kind it reads; it has versions, as a reference table has.
software that reads and writes pods as the vocabulary requires; this package is one.
a judgment that its members are one thing, so answers show them once.
a kit's pod saved as files a web page can read.
the graph and conversion findings a kit keeps for each document its story imports, as the Bridge made them.
of a pod or a file, encrypted on disk so that only the secret opens it.
the six words that open an encrypted pod; `sixWords()` draws them from the EFF long word list, a public list of 7,776 easy-to-type words.
drawn by a random generator started from a stated number, so a failing case can be drawn again.
the place in a document an arrival was read from.
one of the reference tables across its versions, such as RxNorm's product ingredients.
one stretch in which a writer has a pod open. (An entry session is another thing: the act of entering records.)
one hash over the paths and bytes of the files of the set, the same in whatever order they were added.
the W3C's Shapes Constraint Language, in which the vocabulary's shapes are written.
the vocabulary's requirements on what a record, a judgment or a file of a pod must state, written in SHACL, the W3C language for checking data.
the set of files a pod held as one act left it, which names the snapshot before it as a git commit names its parent.
one hospital server, or one document, whose records an export holds.
the W3C query language for data written as statements, as Turtle writes them; `pod.ask()` runs an app's own SPARQL SELECT.
a constraint of a shape written as a SPARQL query, each row of which is one thing wrong with the focus node `$this`.
in a test, a fast hash used in place of Argon2id where no real key is under test.
one scripted action on a pod, such as making it, an import, an entry session or a judgment, named by a letter and a number such as `J10`.
what holds graphs and runs SPARQL over them; here Oxigraph.
the steps taken with one made-up patient's exports, in order.
the person a pod is about.
the act a writer writes after it received another writer's files; its snapshot merges the heads that arrived.
what a reference table's rows say, such as product ingredients or vaccine groups; the vocabulary declares each kind.
one release of a reference table: the rows a table kind holds as of one date, named by an IRI the pod's files use.
what a shape names to say which nodes it checks: a class, the subjects or objects of a property, or one node.
one word the vocabulary defines, named by an IRI, a web-style identifier such as `https://ns.cascadeprotocol.org/cascade#allergen`.
the files a pod works out from its records after every step: its views and its manifest.
the files of a pod that a set hash covers; the layout says which, and an act's own file and a sync's file are left out of the hash their snapshot states.
the party that passed a document on without writing it, as Apple Health does a hospital's record.
a check that turns red on a change someone should look at, not on a fault in the package.
a W3C text format for writing statements in the vocabulary's terms; `pod.enter()` and `pod.judge()` take it.
the file in which a pod lists, for each class of thing, the file or folder that holds it, so that another app can find the pod's views.
of a table version a pod names: not among the tables the pod is opened with.
a store read with some of its graphs as the default graph.
the `Refusal` thrown when a pod does not open with the secret given, or with none; its `outcome` gives the reason, such as `incorrect secret`.
the beginning that every IRI of one code system's codes shares.
a test case the vocabulary publishes for every runtime: inputs, and the result each must give, such as a name.
what a record says at one time; when a source changes a record, the pod keeps the old version and adds a new one. (Of a reference table or the runtime, "version" has its everyday meaning.)

a pod's records of one kind, such as medications, as its judgments leave them: one line for each thing however many sources reported it. A named question such as `pod/My medication history` returns a view's rows.
one thing in a view, such as one medication or one lab result: the records that are one thing, shown as one. A row names it in `entry`, by an IRI that ends in `#` and 64 hexadecimal digits.
cascade-vocabulary, the project that defines the words health data is written in, the requirements every pod meets, and a set of ready-made questions.
the portable compiled form the Bridge is built in, which runs in a browser and in Node.
a thread a web page or Node starts to run code apart from the main one.
one app or device that writes to a pod; two writers hold copies of it and exchange files.
